page.layout: One page of text: running head and title at top centre, page number top left; an engraving in the centre; a verse of two couplets below the engraving; a catchword-like word "Pie" at the lower right, beside the verse.

l.i: Quod sumus & gerimus diuino munere constat:
Ex nobis aliud non nisi bulla sumus.
Ergo cuiq; fiet magnæ sua lectio curæ,
Vt domus officiis fiet bene iuncta suis.

page.notes: The engraving shows three figures standing on a globe beneath clouds: a soldier with a sword at left, a bishop-like figure holding a book and crozier in the centre, and a civilian with a forked tool at right; a landscape is depicted on the globe. The word "Pie" at lower right is set apart from the verse and is treated here as a printed word, not as a catchword. The running head "EMBLEMA" is in small capitals above the title. The title line is in italic capitals with the Q and V of the Latin set in swash forms. Long s is written as s throughout the verse.
